candidate_relations.reason: CD1a and S-100 negativity contradict Hand-Schuller-Christian LCH despite diabetes insipidus.
Flexural reddish-brown papules with diabetes insipidus and CD68-positive CD1a-negative foamy histiocytes are classic xanthoma disseminatum.
The widespread histiocytic papules and granulomatous biopsy are not features of autoimmune polyendocrinopathy.
Seven years of polydipsia and polyuria with established central diabetes insipidus represents associated pituitary involvement.
The diffuse symmetric flexural distribution and endocrine involvement differ from typical solitary juvenile xanthogranuloma.
Diabetes insipidus is a documented systemic association but does not name the cutaneous histiocytosis.
The biopsy lacked both CD1a and S-100 expression required for Langerhans-cell lineage.
No symmetric long-bone osteosclerosis or perirenal infiltration was reported in this skin-predominant teen.
There was no destructive arthritis, periungual papules, or ground-glass histiocytes supporting multicentric reticulohistiocytosis.
Multisystem symptoms are present, but CD1a-negative S-100-negative histiocytes exclude cutaneous LCH.
Skin and pituitary involvement make a multisystem histiocytosis plausible, but the specific xanthoma disseminatum phenotype is lost.
Cutaneous lesions plus endocrine disease fit this broad description without identifying their shared histiocytic cause.
Growth retardation suggests pituitary dysfunction, but no growth-hormone measurement establishes deficiency.
A seven-year acquired papular eruption with histiocytic biopsy does not indicate congenital glycosylation failure.
No hepatosplenomegaly, neurologic regression, or lipid-storage cells supported Niemann-Pick disease.
Hypothyroidism was diagnosed alongside central diabetes insipidus but does not explain the CD68-positive skin infiltrate.
Lesions and endocrine symptoms began in childhood, conflicting with adult-onset scope.
Multisystem inflammation is compatible only generically and omits the defining non-Langerhans histiocytosis.
The biopsy contained foam cells and was CD68 positive without noncaseating sarcoidal granulomas or thoracic disease.
Diabetes insipidus, hypothyroidism, and skin xanthomas do not constitute MEN1-associated endocrine tumors.
